doc_summary: The post describes training models on CHIVE-generated, counterfactually grounded investigations of in-the-wild behavior to predict counterfactual outcomes and self-explain; counterfactual prediction generalizes to held-out settings, open-ended explanation does not, and no privileged access is found. The paper favors discovered, verifiable causes over inserted hints and objective counterfactual re-runs as ground truth.

items.claim: Prefers ground truth from actually re-running the model under counterfactual interventions over plausible-sounding or judged explanations, because causal claims about behavior can then be verified objectively.
items.quote: The counterfactual outcome labels are also cheap and objective to verify, because the label of a counterfactual claim comes from actually re-running the model under the intervention and checking whether the behavior rate moved.

items.claim: Prefers in-the-wild prompts with discovered causes over inserted known cues (hint settings) because hint settings are narrow, with one known feature and one predefined behavior, unlike real deployment questions.
items.quote: The setting is very narrow, as there is one known input feature (the hint) and one predefined output behavior (whether the model followed it). The questions we actually want self-explanations to answer in deployment

items.claim: Distrusts generalization claims that only transfer between near-identical formats (e.g. one hint format to another) and demands transfer to a genuinely held-out task.
items.quote: To our knowledge, no training for causal self-explanations has been shown to generalize to a genuinely held-out task. Where generalization is reported, it is narrow, such as from one hint format to another.

items.claim: Uses real-world data (WildChat) and screens for surprising or confusing behavior rather than generating synthetic or random edits, because random edits are either meaningless or trivially unsurprising.
items.quote: But it is very difficult to programmatically generate inputs with known counterfactual causes that are *interesting*. The average random edit to a text document is either meaningless (the behavior doesn't change) or changes the behavior in a completely unsurprising way

items.claim: Distrusts uplift results that may be confounded by distillation from a stronger investigator or by a capability gap, so it adds a self-investigation control.
items.quote: when a much more capable model runs the investigation, an uplift in the trained target may simply reflect distillation from the larger model, rather than anything specific to the training-data setup.

items.claim: Prefers a controlled cross-model test (privileged access) over assuming introspection because a model may merely learn a good prior over what the model tends to do.
items.quote: The model may be gaining some form of introspective privileged access to its own processing, or it may simply be learning a good prior over what this model tends to do, which any capable model could in principle learn from the same data.

items.claim: Limits claims to what was verified, restricting evaluation to counterfactual outcomes since open-ended explanation correctness is fuzzy, and avoiding the introspection label when the evidence doesn't support it.
items.quote: We therefore use the term "self-explanation" to describe the task format of training a model to report on its own behavior, and not as a claim that the skill is introspective.

items.claim: Uses an independent judge checking each explanation against the full experimental record, and includes negative evidence (hypotheses that failed) in reports, to make evidence more convincing.
items.quote: An independent judge verifies each explanation against the full experimental record.

items.claim: Treats weak or null results honestly, reading them as possible evidence that training struggles to elicit uniquely model-accessible information, while noting surprise and uncertainty.
items.quote: Together, these results suggest that training struggles to elicit information which is uniquely available to the model itself.

items.claim: Proposes using the datasets as a testbed and directly RL-ing against the counterfactual simulatability metric as future work.
items.quote: We think datasets such as ours are a promising testbed for future self-explanation methods (a natural direction is to directly RL against the counterfactual simulatability metric).
